source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Investigate the clinical decision-support failure and continue systematic testing, monitoring, and improvement of EHR alerts and order-entry safeguards.","B":"Disable all medication alerts permanently after this event, because one missed warning shows that clinical decision support creates more risk than benefit.","C":"Return immediately to paper-only ordering throughout the organization, because an isolated EHR alert failure proves electronic ordering cannot be made safe.","D":"Leave the system unchanged if no second failure occurs, because clinical decision-support tools do not require ongoing monitoring after implementation."}}
source_row.rationale: An allergy-alert failure is a patient-safety signal that warrants investigation and ongoing evaluation of the clinical decision-support system. Option A matches ONC SAFER guidance on safe design, implementation, use, and monitoring of CPOE and CDS. Option B overreacts by disabling all alerts rather than correcting the failure. Option C abandons electronic ordering based on a single defect instead of improving the system. Option D ignores the need for ongoing monitoring after implementation.

source_row.stem: An electronic health record fails to display an expected allergy alert during medication ordering. Which organizational response best supports patient safety?
